# Frozen pre-daemon bulk capture

`bulk-operation-cases.capture.js` preserves the exact original generator bytes (SHA-256 `45a1c0b5c0e318fcef2891d413c62a8e925f67794c84503ca788c667ee4b7504`). Its imports and capture logic belong to the original test path on source snapshot `35cbe14f98afd4260733cc2fdcce30676d6b419e`, base `cb8f523fac8f3688c3acf0ffe2d67c66f00e4752`. It is an archive artifact, outside ordinary test discovery because its filename is not a test filename, and must never run against the migrated native facade. Historical recapture requires an explicitly authorized disposable remote checkout of that pinned source, restoring these exact bytes to the original test path; ordinary verification requires no historical Git objects.

The original active test path verifies the frozen JSON SHA-256 `4b99208a0f1f0c5b3a2d7a96919c3c8f35747764346c02bf3d660c0f315475b8`, generator digest, source provenance, ten grouping cases and 25-run inventory. It compares every saved grouping case with the actual current `groupBulkTargets` helper and rejects generation requests. The fixture is never regenerated from the native implementation.

Native behavioral replacement remains explicit: `src-core/tests/bulk_parity.rs` checks frozen grouping, legacy resume and initial-persistence observations. `src-core/tests/bulk_worker.rs` checks four effect orders plus thirteen applicable failure/copy/cancel traces and preserves the intentional stricter-proof divergence. These are 17 applicable ordered traces, not a claim that all 25 legacy runs or the opaque legacy purge trace match.
